item.title: How Government Policy Influences Business Incubation and Acceleration Systems: Insights from National Policy Frameworks
item.content:encoded:
This special issue examines how government policies shape the development, effectiveness, and sustainability of business incubation and acceleration systems across different national contexts. The focus is on understanding the policy frameworks that influence the structure, operations, and outcomes of these critical entrepreneurial support mechanisms.

Appel publié par Technovation. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Government policy frameworks and their impact on business incubation ecosystems
  • Regulatory environments that support or hinder business acceleration
  • National policies promoting entrepreneurship and startup development
  • Policy mechanisms for fostering innovation and economic growth
  • Comparative analysis of government support systems across countries
  • Public sector investment in incubation and acceleration infrastructure
  • Policy barriers and enablers in startup ecosystems

Timeline

  • March 31, 2027: Submission deadline

item.title: Technological sovereignty and innovation policy: strategies for governing and securing critical technologies
item.content:encoded:
This special issue seeks to explore the emerging concept of technological sovereignty and its implications for innovation policy, particularly in the context of securing critical technologies in an increasingly multipolar world. The special issue invites contributions that examine how nations and regions are developing strategies to govern, protect, and advance their technological capabilities while maintaining competitiveness and security.

Submissions are welcome that address theoretical frameworks, empirical analyses, and policy recommendations related to technological sovereignty, critical technology governance, innovation ecosystems, supply chain resilience, international technology competition, and the balance between openness and protection in innovation systems.
